record.paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
record.original_question: Is every smooth Gushel-Mukai Fano variety K-stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Any smooth Gushel-Mukai Fano variety X is K-stable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Gushel–Mukai (GM) variety is a smooth $n$-dimensional complex projective variety obtained as a dimensionally transverse intersection
$$X = \mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \cap \mathbb{P}(W) \cap Q,$$
where $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5) \subset \mathbb{P}^9$ is the Grassmannian of 2-planes in a 5-dimensional vector space embedded by Plücker, $\mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is the projective cone over it, $\mathbb{P}(W) \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is a linear subspace, and $Q$ is a quadric hypersurface. Smooth GM varieties of dimension $n \in \{3,4,5,6\}$ are Fano. Recall that a Fano manifold $X$ is K-stable if for every nontrivial special test configuration $(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{L}) \to \mathbb{A}^1$ for $(X, -K_X)$, the generalized Donaldson–Futaki invariant satisfies $\mathrm{DF}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{L}) > 0$.

Prove or disprove: every smooth Gushel–Mukai Fano variety (of dimension $3$, $4$, $5$, or $6$) is K-stable.
artifact.status_search_result: All smooth Gushel–Mukai threefolds are known to be K-stable (Araujo–Zhuang and related work). In dimensions 4, 5, and 6, K-stability has been established for general (and general special) GM manifolds by Liu–Wang (2024), but the full statement for every smooth GM Fano variety in dimensions 4–6 is not yet proven, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: K-stability of special Gushel-Mukai manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: a general special GM manifold of dimension 4, 5, or 6 is K-stable (Theorem 1.1); all the smooth GM threefolds are K-stable [AZ21]
status_evidence.claim: K-stability is proven for all smooth GM threefolds and for general (special) GM manifolds in dimensions 4, 5, 6, but not yet for all smooth GM Fano varieties in those higher dimensions.
